Plot Outside-Polygon PCF Envelopes for All Cell-Type Pairs

plot_pcf_outside_pair_envelopes.Rd

Usage

plot_pcf_outside_pair_envelopes(
  seurat_obj,
  polygons,
  celltype_col,
  fov_name = "fov",
  min_cells = 10,
  include_self_pairs = FALSE,
  ordered_pairs = FALSE,
  nsim,
  bw = 10,
  window_obj = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  res = 150,
  verbose = TRUE,
  tissue_window = c("concave", "convex", "bbox"),
  null_model = c("csr", "band_permutation"),
  band_width = 25,
  envelope_type = c("global", "pointwise"),
  r_range = NULL
)

Arguments

seurat_obj

Seurat object with spatial coordinates.

polygons

sf polygon object representing ROIs.

celltype_col

Metadata column containing cell type labels.

fov_name

Field of view/image name passed to `Seurat::GetTissueCoordinates`.

min_cells

Minimum number of cells required per cell type.

include_self_pairs

Logical; include same-type pairs.

ordered_pairs

Logical; if `TRUE`, computes ordered pairs.

nsim

Number of simulations for envelopes (required). Global envelopes have significance level `1 / (nsim + 1)` (0.05 for `nsim = 19`, 0.01 for `nsim = 99`); pointwise envelopes have `2 / (nsim + 1)` at each r.

bw

Kernel bandwidth (microns) passed to `pcfcross`. Use the same value as in [calculate_pcf_outside_summary()] so the envelope curves match the heatmap values. `NULL` uses the `spatstat` default.

window_obj

Optional `spatstat.geom::owin` tissue window; tumor polygons are subtracted from it.

file

Optional base PNG file path (e.g. `"pcf_envelopes.png"`). One PNG is written per pair, with the pair name appended to the file stem.

width, height

PNG size in inches.

res

PNG resolution in pixels per inch.

verbose

Logical; print progress messages.

tissue_window

Tissue outline used when `window_obj` is `NULL`: `"concave"` (default; concave hull of all cells), `"convex"`, or `"bbox"`. Tumor polygons are always removed from the window.

null_model

Null model for the envelopes: `"csr"` or `"band_permutation"`. See Details.

band_width

Band width (microns) for `null_model = "band_permutation"`.

envelope_type

`"global"` (default) or `"pointwise"`. See Details.

r_range

Distance range `c(lower, upper)` in microns. `upper` sets the largest distance computed (default: the `spatstat` default maximum). For global envelopes the test covers `[lower, upper]`; `lower` defaults to `bw` (or 5

Named list of envelope objects. Each has attributes `null_model`, `envelope_type`, `alpha` (significance level), and `r_range`; global envelopes also have `p_value` (MAD test). Computes and plots envelope-based pair correlation curves for all requested cell-type pairs outside polygons. When `file` is provided, each pair is saved as its own PNG named `<file stem>_<type1>_vs_<type2>.png`. Two null models are available: * `"csr"`: complete spatial randomness. Points are placed uniformly at random in the outside-tumor window with independent labels. This tests clustering of the cells themselves as well as co-localization, and tissue is rarely uniform. * `"band_permutation"`: cell positions are kept and cell-type labels are permuted among cells in the same distance band from the tumor boundary (bands of width `band_width`). This tests whether two types co-localize beyond what their shared distance-to-tumor gradients explain. Use `band_width = Inf` for plain random labelling across all outside cells.Two envelope types are available: * `"global"` (default): a simultaneous envelope (`spatstat` `global = TRUE`, maximum absolute deviation). The observed curve leaves it anywhere in `r_range` with probability `1 / (nsim + 1)` under the null, so it can be read across all distances at once without multiple testing. The band has the same width at every distance. A matching MAD test p-value, computed from the same simulations, is stored in the `p_value` attribute. With `null_model = "band_permutation"`, `2 * nsim` permutations are run: the second set estimates the null mean curve. * `"pointwise"`: separate envelopes at each distance, with a two-sided significance level of `2 / (nsim + 1)` at each single r. Checking many distances inflates the false-positive rate.
